texts.title: The Hustings
texts.body: The consuls are elected at the turn's end and the Reach's houses are speaking in the colonnade: promises to the squares, promises to the salons, wine for the undecided. {self.name} is asked what {self.house} stands for.

choices.promise_the_old_blood: Speak for order and the old families.
choices.buy_the_hall: Hire the hall, the wine and the band (8 credits).
choices.stay_away: Stay away and let the record speak.

texts.title: The Consulship
texts.body: The Senate has elected {self.name} consul. The lictors — such as the Reach has — fall in at the door; the clerk brings the seal; the parties that did not vote for {self.house} are already composing their objections.

choices.reward_the_party: Spend the first session rewarding your voters.

texts.title: The Veto Falls
texts.body: A consul has struck {self.house}'s motion from the docket before the vote. The clerk is apologetic; the consul is not. The chamber is watching to see how {self.name} takes it.

choices.take_it_to_the_squares: Read the vetoed motion in the squares.
choices.wait_for_the_term: Wait for the consul's term to end.
choices.court_the_other_consul: Dine with the other consul (1 influence).

texts.title: The Term Ends
texts.body: {self.house}'s consulship is over: the seal goes back to the clerk and the chair to whoever the parties have chosen. A consul who leaves well is remembered; one who leaves badly is remembered longer.

choices.a_triumph_of_sorts: A procession through the capital (5 credits).
choices.keep_the_lictors: Keep the lictors on, out of habit.
